discussion: I need to add port behavior documentation with doctest examples to the urlparse section of Doc/library/urllib.parse.rst. The previous patch was rejected due to ambiguous old text (appeared in both urlparse and urlsplit sections). I'll use a longer unique anchor that includes 'As is the case with all named tuples' which only appears in the urlparse section. I'll insert the new port validation explanation and doctest examples between the existing port paragraph and the 'Unmatched square brackets' paragraph.

operation.new:
Reading the :attr:`port` attribute will raise a :exc:`ValueError` if
   an invalid port is specified in the URL.  See section
   :ref:`urlparse-result-object` for more information on the result object.

   Port validation is deferred: constructing a result object with
   :func:`urlsplit` or :func:`urlparse` never raises for port problems.
   The port value is checked only when the :attr:`port` attribute is
   accessed.  A valid port is an empty string (yielding :const:`None`)
   or an ASCII decimal integer in the range 0 through 65535 inclusive.
   If the port string is not a sequence of ASCII digits, or the resulting
   integer is outside 0-65535, accessing :attr:`port` raises
   :exc:`ValueError`.

   .. doctest::
      :options: +NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE

      >>> from urllib.parse import urlsplit, urlparse
      >>> urlsplit("http://example.com:0/").port
      0
      >>> urlsplit("http://example.com:65535/").port
      65535
      >>> urlsplit("http://example.com:65536/").port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port out of range 0-65535
      >>> urlsplit("http://example.com:-1/").port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as '-1'
      >>> urlsplit("http://example.com:abc/").port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as 'abc'
      >>> urlsplit("http://example.com/").port is None
      True
      >>> urlsplit("http://example.com:/").port is None
      True
      >>> urlparse("http://example.com:65536/").port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port out of range 0-65535

   Unmatched square brackets in the :attr:`netloc` attribute will raise a
   :exc:`ValueError`.

   Characters in the :attr:`netloc` attribute that decompose under NFKC
   normalization (as used by the IDNA encoding) into any of ``/``, ``?``,
   ``#``, ``@``, or ``:`` will raise a :exc:`ValueError`. If the URL is
   decomposed before parsing, no error will be raised.

   As is the case with all named tuples, the subclass has a few additional methods
